report_name: North Korean 'PolinRider' APT Hits 100+ Open-Source Repos in Major Supply Chain Attack

threat_actors.name: Lazarus Group
threat_actors.description: The North Korean advanced persistent threat (APT) group responsible for the PolinRider campaign, operating through its subgroup Famous Chollima.

threat_actors.name: Famous Chollima
threat_actors.description: A subgroup of the Lazarus Group directly attributed to carrying out the PolinRider supply chain attack campaign.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
attack_patterns.description: The core technique of the PolinRider campaign, where attackers compromise legitimate open-source packages to inject malicious code, affecting downstream developers and projects.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Attackers gained initial access to open-source repositories by using the compromised credentials of legitimate package maintainers.

attack_patterns.name: Credentials In Files
attack_patterns.description: The final payload, an info-stealer, is designed to find and exfiltrate developer secrets and cloud tokens from credential files on the compromised developer's machine.

attack_patterns.name: Disable or Modify Tools
attack_patterns.description: Attackers rewrote the Git version history of compromised repositories to make malicious commits appear older and part of routine maintenance, thereby evading detection from security analysts and code reviewers.

attack_patterns.name: Dead Drop Resolver
attack_patterns.description: The malware uses public blockchain infrastructure as a dead-drop resolver to retrieve its final encrypted payload, making the C2 mechanism resilient to takedowns.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Phishing was a likely method used to compromise the accounts of legitimate open-source package maintainers.

attack_patterns.name: Credential Stuffing
attack_patterns.description: Credential stuffing was a likely method used to compromise the accounts of legitimate open-source package maintainers.

attack_patterns.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
attack_patterns.description: Attackers hid obfuscated malicious code within the legitimate source code of the compromised software packages.

malware.name: PolinRider RAT/Infostealer
malware.description: The final payload delivered by the PolinRider campaign. It is a remote-access trojan (RAT) and information stealer designed to harvest sensitive data such as developer secrets, cloud tokens (AWS, Azure), and cryptocurrency wallets.

malware.name: PolinRider JavaScript Loader
malware.description: A concealed JavaScript loader injected into compromised open-source packages. It executes upon installation and connects to a public blockchain to retrieve the final payload.

tools.name: git
tools.description: The git version control system was used by the attackers to rewrite the history of compromised repositories to hide their malicious commits.

campaigns.name: PolinRider
campaigns.description: A large-scale, sophisticated supply chain attack campaign targeting the open-source software ecosystem by compromising the accounts of trusted package maintainers to inject malware.

identities.name: npm
identities.description: The npm (JavaScript) package registry was one of the platforms targeted in the PolinRider campaign, where compromised packages were published.

identities.name: Go
identities.description: The Go package index was one of the platforms targeted in the PolinRider campaign, where compromised modules were published.

identities.name: Packagist
identities.description: The Packagist (PHP) package registry was one of the platforms targeted in the PolinRider campaign, where compromised packages were published.

infrastructure.name: PolinRider Blockchain C2
infrastructure.description: Public blockchain infrastructure used as a dead-drop resolver to fetch the final payload for the PolinRider malware, making it resilient to takedowns.

indicators.name: PolinRider C2 Blockchain Resolver Detection
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Suspicious DNS Query to Blockchain Explorer During Build
id: 2b8c5a1f-3d4e-4b1a-9c8d-7e6f5a4b3c2d
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS queries to public blockchain explorers from processes related to software builds or package installation. This may indicate PolinRider supply chain attack activity.
references:
  - https://www.scworld.com/news/north-korean-polinrider-supply-chain-attack-targets-108-unique-repos
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-07
tags:
  - attack.t1102.001
  - attack.command_and_control
level: medium
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_domains:
    QueryName|contains:
      - 'etherscan.io'
      - 'bscscan.com'
  selection_process:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\go.exe'
      - '\php.exe'
      - '\composer.phar'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate developer tools or packages that interact with blockchain explorers for non-malicious reasons.
indicators.description: Detects network connections from build tools to public blockchain explorers, a TTP used in the PolinRider campaign to fetch payloads.

indicators.name: Suspicious Credential Access by Package Manager
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Credential Access by Package Manager
id: 8f9a0b1c-2d3e-4f5a-6b7c-8d9e0f1a2b3c
status: experimental
description: Detects package manager processes accessing sensitive credential files. This may indicate a compromised dependency attempting to steal secrets, as seen in the PolinRider campaign.
references:
  - https://www.scworld.com/news/north-korean-polinrider-supply-chain-attack-targets-108-unique-repos
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-07
tags:
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.credential_access
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_process:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\go.exe'
      - '\php.exe'
      - '\composer.phar'
  selection_files:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '.aws\credentials'
      - '.ssh\'
      - '.git-credentials'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate developer tools or scripts that need to access these credentials as part of their normal function.
indicators.description: Detects package manager processes reading sensitive credential files, a behavior associated with the PolinRider infostealer payload.

relationships.target_name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools

relationships.source_name: Suspicious Credential Access by Package Manager
